newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Holiday-hit Brussels bourse seeks inspiration.
newsitem.headline: Holiday-hit Brussels bourse seeks inspiration.

text.p: The Brussels bourse, becalmed by holiday absences but supported by the rising dollar and low interest rates, searched for inspiration on Monday but with little hope of finding any in the near future, traders said.
"It is very, very poor. It is dreary," one trader said. "There has been less than half a billion francs of business."
The Bel-20 index of blue-chip shares was 3.06 points or 0.12 percent higher at 2,495.47 at 0900 GMT, with 11 gainers, three unchanged and six losers.
Traders said the market would remain in limbo until the first batch of half year results from the larger companies.
Retailer Colruyt was a notable loser, down 375 francs or 1.9 percent to 18,975 francs after BBL downrated the share to sell from hold following its strong recent performance and a company visit.
Among the gainers, electronics firm Barco put on 1.1 percent to 7,570 francs.
Generale Bank said in its market commentary that the firm's recent purchase of Danish company RE was interesting and profitable, but would add relatively little to sales.
